sections.heading: C — Pavement markings and lane controls
sections.markdown:
## C — Pavement markings and lane controls

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Pavement lines and symbols separate traffic lanes and indicate permitted passing, lane changes and turning use. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Pavement markings can designate pedestrian crossings and the stopping position for a sign or signal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
A continuous line beside the roadway identifies its edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
White lane lines separate streams of traffic moving the same way. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
A broken white lane line allows a lane change after checking that the movement is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
A solid white lane line calls for staying in the lane unless a special circumstance requires a change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A01
For a stop required by a sign or signal, stop before the vehicle reaches the stop line or crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
A crosswalk identifies the place where pedestrians cross the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
Drivers must yield to pedestrians already in a crosswalk or about to step into it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian crossing can exist even without painted crosswalk markings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
Yellow lane lines separate vehicles moving toward each other. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
A broken yellow center line permits passing when the maneuver is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
With a paired solid and broken yellow center line, a driver on the solid-line side may not pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A01
With a paired solid and broken yellow center line, a driver beside the broken line may pass when safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A01
A double solid yellow center line prohibits passing from either side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A01
A driver may cross a solid yellow line to enter a driveway when the turn is safe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

Misconceptions: white lines separate traffic traveling the same way; yellow lines divide opposing directions.
Mnemonics: white follows the flow; yellow faces opposing flow.
Glossary: reversible means the lane direction changes; reserved means the lane has a specified permitted use.
Dynamic facts: overhead lane signals and posted occupancy restrictions must be checked at the time of use.

sections.heading: C2 — Pavement markings and lane controls
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Pavement markings and lane controls

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A02
A reversible lane carries traffic in opposite directions at different times. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A02
Reversible lanes are commonly marked by paired broken yellow lines. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A02
Before entering a reversible lane, check the current lane-use signs or signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A02
A green overhead arrow permits use of the lane directly below it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A02
A red overhead X prohibits driving in the lane below it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A02
A flashing yellow overhead X limits the lane to turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A02
A steady yellow overhead X warns of a lane-use change and calls for leaving the lane as soon as safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A02
A reserved lane is identified by signs describing the permitted use and often by a white diamond. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A02
A lane labeled Transit or Bus is reserved for buses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A02
A lane labeled Bicycle is reserved for bicycle travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A02
HOV means high-occupancy vehicles and identifies a lane for vehicles carrying more than one person. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A02
The sign for an HOV lane specifies the required occupancy and the days and hours of the restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A02
An HOV three sign requires at least three occupants in the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A02
A shared middle lane is used by traffic from either direction for left turns or permitted U-turns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A02
Alternating left-turn arrows show the movements permitted from a shared middle lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A02
A shared middle lane is bounded on each side by a solid yellow line paired with a broken yellow line. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A02
Some shared middle lanes become reversible during peak traffic periods, so entry requires checking that the lane is available and safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A02
When signs and markings do not assign lane use, general driving, passing and turning rules determine the lane to use. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0012]
